assignment: Bounded independent source-quality review of PayrollRules.AssertTransition; no shared registry edits, tests, runtime, or data operations.

source_behavior.semantics: Pure membership check against the transition dictionary. Missing/unknown source status and unsupported edge throw DomainException; self-transitions are implicitly forbidden. No persistence or monetary side effects in this domain method.
source_behavior.receipt_reasoning_check: The saved receipt correctly enumerates Approved->Paid and the terminal states, and links generic status transition to FIN-006. I verified the current source table and method body match its stable ID, signature and span.

generic_api.behavior: POST /api/payroll-runs/{runId}/transition replaces PayrollRunId from route and invokes TransitionPayrollHandler.HandleAsync; DomainException maps to 422.
generic_api.request_type: src/Falah.Application/Employees/PayrollRequests.cs:26; TransitionPayrollRequest carries run ID, string status, actor, and optional approval fields.

generic_handler.behavior: Parses requested enum case-insensitively; requires employees_manage; loads current run; calls AssertTransition; adds payroll_approve approval only for target Approved; assigns run.Status and reviewer/approval metadata; calls SaveChanges. For target Paid, this handler has no payment-account validation, open-day gate, treasury movement, employee PayrollSettlement entries, PaidAtUtc, or invocation of PayPayrollHandler.

dedicated_payment_counterevidence.behavior: Separate /pay workflow requires Approved and payroll_pay, validates positive total/open business day, uses transaction-held protected-balance lock and idempotency journal, posts one treasury movement and positive per-line employee settlement debits, then sets Paid metadata and commits atomically. This is the supported monetary payout path; it does not make the generic status-only path monetary.

call_path_and_financial_effect.permission_boundary: The generic route is not anonymous in handler design: it authorizes employees_manage. But the Approved-only payroll_approve gate does not apply to Paid target, so an employees_manage actor who can call the endpoint can select Paid if the run is Approved. Actual use is unverified.

domain_test.coverage: Theory accepts Draft->Calculated, Draft->Cancelled, Calculated->Reviewed, Reviewed->Approved, Approved->Paid; rejects Draft->Reviewed and Paid/Cancelled->Draft. It does not enumerate every invalid edge, every Cancelled edge, unknown enum values, or assert handler side effects.

integration_test.coverage: The lifecycle-named integration case actually transitions Draft->Calculated->Reviewed->Approved and stops at Approved. Separate payment test exercises /pay and checks movement/settlement. No test calls generic /transition with target Paid and then asserts absence of monetary records.

counterevidence: There is a dedicated atomic payout path with explicit safeguards, so not all payroll payment is status-only.
UI normal next-status flow is documented in existing FIN-006 provenance as stopping at Approved; this reduces evidence of ordinary UI accidental invocation, but does not remove API reachability.
Generic route requires employees_manage; this is a permission boundary, not evidence that Paid has payout effects.
tests_and_counterevidence.static_limitations: No test/runtime/DB calls were run. This establishes source-level reachability and missing handler side effects, not a real operator action, unpaid payroll incident, authorization bypass, or database state observed in production.

finding_disposition.reason: The status-only Approved->Paid transition is already canonical FIN-006. This review confirms the domain edge, route, generic handler behavior, distinct monetary payout path, and test gap; it does not add a separate root cause or duplicate finding.
finding_disposition.required_follow_up: Keep FIN-006 as a source-confirmed behavior. Owner/policy decision: remove Paid from generic transition edges or make the transition delegate to/require committed payout evidence. Add an integration regression test proving generic transition cannot leave a run Paid without treasury movement and line settlements, while dedicated /pay still commits Paid atomically. Runtime incidence remains unverified.
